vault.createIntro: Entries are encrypted before they go on-chain permanently (only ciphertext ever reaches the chain). Set a recovery passphrase:
vault.createHint: In brief: a random data key encrypts all entries, and the key itself is wrapped by two independent channels — your passphrase and your wallet signature. Everyday unlocking is just a wallet signature; if the wallet is lost, the keystore file + passphrase recover everything. Full principles and do-it-yourself verification:

about.feeIntro: PermaDrive publishes at the protocol level: what you pay is what you store, and the data is kept **permanently**. The official AutoDrive service prices storage in credits (expiring after 90 days, purchase requires a Google login). Both PermaDrive fees below are read live from the chain (consensus storage fee + FileRegistry quote); the official price is the 2026-10 measured figure.
about.connectingRates: Connecting to the consensus chain for live rates…
about.feeFormula: max(minFee, size × feePerByte) — overpayment is refunded automatically
about.paramsValue: feePerByte {0} wei/byte · minFee {1} AI3 · cap {2} AI3/byte (hard anti-rug ceiling)
about.sovereigntyNote: The dev fee is charged on the value-added point of one-click cross-device recovery; not registering leaves the data itself untouched — files can always be fetched for free with their manifest or by scanning the chain directly (no involvement of this project). Registration fees go straight to the project treasury and fund the maintenance of the public frontend and tooling.
about.featureFilesDesc: Any file packed as IPLD and published on-chain, archived permanently by the farmer network; the manifest is the retrieval credential
about.featureNotesDesc: Append-only text records; every save is a new immutable version, the version chain is held in the on-chain registry
about.featureNotesCost: per version: storage fee + dev fee (small texts usually hit the 0.01 AI3 floor)
about.featureVaultDesc: Entries are AES-256-GCM encrypted as one envelope before publishing (only ciphertext reaches the chain); one wallet-signature unlock, keystore file as the recovery fallback
about.featureVaultCost: per save: storage fee + dev fee (you control the registration cadence)
about.plaintextNote: "My files" and notes are published in the clear (permanently public); private text belongs in the encrypted vault — principles and do-it-yourself verification in
about.sovAccountsDesc: wallet signatures are the identity; no personal information is collected
about.sovBackendDesc: fully static frontend; the RPC / indexer dependencies are replaceable public protocol infrastructure
about.sovLockInDesc: manifests are self-contained and shareable; even if this project disappears, any public infrastructure can still retrieve your data in full
about.sovPermanentDesc: published data cannot be deleted (that is what makes version history and undelete possible) — make sure content is fit for public before publishing
about.faqIntro: Answers to the questions that actually matter — including our own mainnet measurements.
about.faq1q: Why does uploading need multiple wallet signatures?
about.faq1a: In the Substrate protocol every transaction is signed independently — there is no "sign once, authorize many" primitive, and a single transaction has a size limit (measured on mainnet: a 2.23 MB batch is accepted, while 4.39 MB is rejected with "would exhaust the block limits"). Large files are therefore sent in ~2 MB batches, one signature each: an 8 MB file takes 5 signatures, 64 MB about 33. For comparison, official AutoDrive carries a single 64 KiB node per transaction — a 1 GB upload means thousands of transactions. Each of our batches is still ~30x larger than theirs.
about.faq2q: Are these limits actually measured, or guessed?
about.faq2a: Measured, on mainnet, on 2026-11-03: an 8 MiB encrypted file was published in 4 confirmed batches (blocks #10247904/#10247920/#10247934/#10247948) for 16.58 AI3 — matching the fee estimate — and the retrieved ciphertext and decrypted plaintext both matched their sha256 baselines. The same measurements confirmed the public gateways cap HTTP request bodies at ~15 MB (16 MB is rejected with 413) and that browsers silently fail to send multi-MB messages over WebSocket — so batches always travel over HTTP, sized at 2 MB with a 10% margin. Under normal conditions you will never see a "chunk rejected" prompt.
about.faq3a: Yes, on two tracks. First, a desktop/CLI edition is already designed: the key lives in a local program that signs automatically — any size, zero popups. (Official AutoDrive achieves the same "invisible multi-signing" by holding your key on their server; we keep the key in your hands.) Second, the batching logic is parameterized: if the network raises its per-transaction limit or you point the app at your own RPC node, the budget can grow accordingly — in the acceptance run it already shrank itself from 4.4 MB to 2.2 MB when the chain said no.
about.faq4q: Where do my fees actually go?
about.faq4a: Three payments, three destinations — no subscription, no account, no intermediary. The storage fee (the large one, ~2.1 AI3/MB) is paid to the consensus chain protocol itself and accrues to the farmer network; PermaDrive never touches it. The directory registration fee (~10% of the storage fee, 0.01 AI3 minimum) flows through the on-chain Registry contract to the project treasury — every payment is recorded in a public FeePaid event, which is also the ledger for a future PERMA token airdrop. Gas is each network's own fee. For comparison, official AutoDrive charges ~4.41 AI3/MB with credits that expire after 90 days: the same 1 GB costs ~2200 AI3 here versus ~4500 AI3 there, expiring.
about.faq5q: If an upload fails, will I be charged twice?
about.faq5a: No. Failures are separated into two classes. "Result unknown" (timeout/disconnect): the app never resends automatically — the transaction may already sit in the pool, resending the same one would hit the dedup ban — it goes to a pending-verification state and is checked on-chain by transaction hash. "Provably not sent" (the node explicitly rejected it, or the gateway returned 413): retrying costs nothing, because the money never left. Measured the same day: a rejected 4.4 MB batch left the balance untouched.
about.faq6a: Yes. Data published to the Subspace consensus chain is archived permanently by the farmer network; the protocol has no delete operation, and the storage fee is paid once — there is nothing to renew. Check before publishing: filenames and sizes are public (encrypted contents are not).
about.faq7q: How do I recover files on a new device — and who can decrypt encrypted files?
about.faq7a: Connect the same wallet on the new device: "My Files" reconciles automatically against the on-chain registry, and the recovery envelope (published alongside the file) carries the wrapped decryption key. Encrypted files use AES-256-GCM: the data key is wrapped by your EVM wallet signature (deterministic, so the same wallet unlocks it anywhere) with an optional passphrase as a backup channel. The key itself never goes on chain — only ciphertext does.

sales.notice: Direct sales: payment goes straight to the seller in the same Auto EVM transaction (10% platform fee included) — no escrow, no platform refunds. Delivery is manual: the seller sends the file key via on-chain private message when online. Buying grants the file itself (no DRM). Only encrypted files make sense. Please rate honestly: up/down votes are on-chain (Auto EVM gas applies), one vote per item per address, editable.

sales.enableReceivingFirst: Enable receiving first (Messages page → Enable receiving) — otherwise the seller cannot deliver the file key.

onboarding.title: Save your first file
onboarding.intro: PermaDrive encrypts your selected file automatically, saves the encrypted data and file index, then lets you verify the result. No advance encryption is needed.
onboarding.privacyHelp: Encryption is recommended and enabled by default. Public uploads cannot be taken back; encrypted files still reveal their name and size.
onboarding.walletHelp: Connect your wallets. PermaDrive generates the file key in your browser and protects it with wallet signatures. You can also add a backup password.
onboarding.uploadHelp: PermaDrive encrypts the file and saves its encrypted data and recovery information on Consensus. Your wallet pays the storage fee.
onboarding.backupHelp: Register the file location with your Auto-EVM directory account, paying the directory and transaction fees. This account can then find the file on another device.
onboarding.verifyHelp: After saving the file index, download the file and automatically check its SHA-256.
onboarding.recoveryReady: Directory account connected, ready to save and retrieve file indexes.
onboarding.recoveryMissing: Connect your Auto-EVM directory account above to protect file keys and save file indexes.
onboarding.sessionNotice: Saving the encrypted data and file index marks the file complete. Download verification is recorded for this page session only.
onboarding.backupConfirm: Save the recovery directory on-chain? You will sign a consensus storage transaction and an EVM directory registration transaction, with separate fees. File contents remain encrypted.
onboarding.unfinishedHelp: Choose “Continue saving file” in the file list to finish recovery information or file indexing. Saved file content is not uploaded again.
onboarding.resolveFirst: The recovery-manifest transaction is still pending verification. Verify it before continuing; do not repay storage fees.
onboarding.localRisk: Complete directory registration promptly. Until then, the information needed to locate your file remains in this browser and is not a reliable backup. Clearing site data, browser data corruption, or switching devices may make the file impossible to find or decrypt. Storage fees already paid cannot be refunded, and earlier work may be lost.

funding.title: Fee estimate
funding.help: Reads fees only. Funding gaps use balance snapshots already shown in the wallet bar, without another balance query or authorization.
funding.missing: Connect wallets and load their balances to calculate funding gaps. Refresh balances in the wallet bar.
funding.bridge: Move AI3 to Auto-EVM with XDM Bridge
funding.warning: Estimated fees may change. Check the amount in your wallet.
funding.insufficientStorage: Consensus usable balance is below the quoted file-storage fee. Add funds before signing.
funding.failed: Fee estimate unavailable. Please retry; no transaction was sent.
funding.insufficientEvm: Auto-EVM balance does not cover directory registration plus gas. Add funds before continuing.
funding.balanceUnknown: Connect wallet or refresh its balance above
funding.chooseFile: Select a file to estimate fees

walletSteps.title: Next wallet action — click to open wallet
walletSteps.unlockHelp: Your EVM wallet will sign a message to unlock this file later. No transaction or fee. Two identical signatures check that this wallet can reproduce the key. Click again for the next step.
walletSteps.upload: Pay and permanently save file and recovery information
walletSteps.uploadHelp: Your consensus wallet signs one transaction per ~2 MB chunk, saving the encrypted file and recovery information. Combined storage estimate: {0} AI3 (check the wallet amount). Storage is permanent. Next, register the directory on EVM to find the file from your wallet on another device.
walletSteps.manifestHelp: Your consensus wallet will sign a separate storage transaction to save file locations and protected key information for recovery on another device. A small additional storage fee applies; check the wallet amount.
walletSteps.registerHelp: Your EVM wallet will sign a directory transaction. Service fee: {0} AI3; estimated gas reserve: {1} AI3. Check the wallet amount. This lets your wallet recover the file list.
walletSteps.cancelled: Further steps stopped. Published content remains saved; you can continue later.
walletSteps.busy: Complete or cancel the current wallet step first.
walletSteps.waitingHelp: Preparing the request, waiting for wallet approval, or awaiting the chain result. Do not click again. Reject in the wallet if needed; this page never approves for you.
walletSteps.preparing: Preparing transaction · waiting for Consensus RPC; the wallet has not been requested yet.
walletSteps.rpcTimeout: Consensus RPC did not respond in time. No transaction was submitted. Wait before retrying.
walletSteps.signTimeout: Wallet signing timed out. This attempt will not broadcast. Reject any outstanding request in your wallet before retrying.
walletSteps.uploadBatch: Save chunk {0}/{1} to the blockchain (consensus storage fee)

resume.directory: Checking whether the file index is already on Auto-EVM…
resume.pending: Checking for an unresolved storage transaction…
resume.timeout: This check timed out. No payment was started by this check. Retry later; unresolved earlier transactions must be verified first.
